newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics strong Q4 seen amid concerns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics strong Q4 seen amid concerns.

text.p: Modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp is expected to report a significant increase in earnings for its fiscal 1996 fourth quarter, but concern about revenue growth has weighed on the stock, securities analysts said.
"I expect it to be a strong quarter, but I don't expect to see any upside surprises," said Amar Senan, an analyst for Volpe, Welty & Co.
U.S. Robotics said it would report earnings for the quarter and year ended September 30 on Monday after the market closes.

According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' fourth quarter estimates is $0.71 a share versus last year's $0.38 (adjusted for a stock split). Analysts said they expect $600 million to $610 million in revenues compared with $293 million last year.
Shares of U.S. Robotics fell 2-7/8 Friday to 60.
"I think that's the irony of the whole story," Senan said. "Management must be tearing their hair out."
U.S. Robotics reported better than expected fiscal 1996 third quarter revenues of $546.8 million, up about 20 percent from the fiscal 1996 second quarter.
The company had forecast average revenue growth of 15 percent during the second half of fiscal 1996 versus the second quarter, which in turn meant fourth quarter alone would be more like 10 percent.
"There is some concern that they will miss the quarter," said James McIlree, an analyst for Southcoast Capital, but he added, "I think they'll make their numbers."
Some analysts reacted to the words of caution last quarter by trimming earnings and revenue estimates and cutting ratings.

Paul Johnson, an analyst for Robertson, Stephens & Co, in an internal phone message to brokers sent on Thursday reiterated concerns stated in his September report in which he initiated coverage with a rating of market performer.
"We remain somewhat concerned that growth rates forecast for the company may be too high," Johnson said in his initial report.
Nonetheless, analysts said they remain largely optimistic over the long run. The company's dominant market share in modems and systems has grown, they said.

Analysts said the announcement that a new modem with 56 kilobit per second capabilities will be available early next year gave the market, plagued with increasing price competition, a boost. The modem will allow for downloading of information at speeds twice as fast as today's common 28.8 kbps modem.
"The sell-through continues to be good, and the systems area has traditionally been strong," said Rakesh Sood, an analyst for Hambrecht & Quist.
"I would have thought the 56-K announcement would have kept some people from buying new modems, but that doesn't seem to be the case," Sood said.
There have been concerns, however, that the 56 kilobit per second downloading speed is too much to expect from traditional telephone lines.
"I expect the company to deal with that in the conference call," Sood said, referring to a call with analysts typically held after earnings are released.
